prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of individual DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B013) to base editing (B024) as a single-achievement prize credited to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli. Round 1 tested my own case and it did not survive intact: Brzezinski, Chabes and Linke each pointed out that the ionizable-lipid credit is spread over Vancouver, Inex, MIT and industrial groups and cannot be cut to three names without choosing between the lipid design and the formulation process, and that the 2023 Medicine prize makes the work look derivative. I raised the same weakness myself, and I cannot rank a candidate first when its own proposer cannot write a clean citation. Base editing has the opposite profile. The chemical step is well defined: a deaminase tethered to a nickase converts C or A at a chosen position without a double-strand break, and the adenine editor required a deaminase evolved to act on DNA because no natural enzyme did. It is quantitative, widely replicated, and in patients. As a physical chemist I value that the idea reduces to one reaction on one base pair. The chair asks whether a Liu-alone credit is defensible. If B024 stands as the only part, the three-person cap no longer forces the exclusion, and Komor and Gaudelli wrote the two decisive papers on the cytidine and adenine editors. In round 1 I said that a first-author trainee should be a laureate only if the committee argues it, and here is the argument: those two papers are the demonstrations the field rests on, the adenine editor in particular is a distinct chemical achievement that required evolving a new activity, and Liu's role as originator of the programme is plain in the record and in the order of the names.
statement.case_against: A single-achievement prize gives up the breadth of the Liu plus Crews and Deshaies pairing, and a Liu, Komor and Gaudelli trio puts two former trainees beside the programme director, which some colleagues will find hard to defend. Base editing may still read as a follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Somfai's point that cytidine and adenosine deamination are old chemistry, with the new part being protein engineering, is not trivial. The Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority question is open, and I do not have the documented record to say whether it changes names or only wording. Durability, bystander and off-target editing are still being measured. Finally, my own field is soft matter, so I am not the best judge of genome-editing biology, and my move away from B013 should not be read as a belief that delivery chemistry is unimportant.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, proposes Liu alone for base editing so that the remaining seats go to Crews and Deshaies for degradation, and says Komor's and Gaudelli's engineering can be credited in the citation text.
responses.response: I follow the arithmetic but not the trade. The pairing is what forces Liu alone, and it rests on a second part (PROTACs) that you yourself say has no approved drug and a credit split between the PROTAC and cereblon glue lineages. A citation text cannot do the work of a name: the laureate list is what the public and the field read, and you accept that the two first-author papers are decisive. If the committee is unwilling to rest B009 on the 2001 concept, I would rather give base editing all three seats than pair it with a part that is still maturing.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the whole prize and calls adenine base editing the strongest evidence of real chemistry, because TadA had to be evolved to act on DNA.
responses.response: I now agree with your configuration, and the adenine-editor point is what moves me: a new catalytic activity on DNA is a chemical result and not just an application of Cas9. I would sharpen it against Somfai's objection: deamination itself is old chemistry, but an evolved deaminase acting on DNA inside a nickase architecture is not, and the citation should speak of base conversion without double-strand cleavage and not of genome editing in general, so it does not reopen the 2020 text. On Target-AID I share your and Aqvist's wish to see the priority record, and I would treat it as a question of wording and possibly of the credited names if the dates put Nishida and Kondo first.

responses.point: Somfai argues that the new chemistry in base editing is largely protein engineering and directed evolution on top of the 2020 CRISPR prize, and proposes pairing a Liu-alone B024 with Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling.
responses.response: This is the strongest case against B024 and I take it seriously. My answer is that evolving an enzyme to act on a substrate it never acted on is itself the chemical problem here, since no natural adenine deaminase works on DNA. I do not think the pairing with B003 helps the citation: it joins a mature synthetic method with a genome-engineering tool that share no theme, and it again forces Liu alone. If the committee prefers C-N coupling it is a defensible single prize, and I do not dispute its attribution or maturity, but I would not pick it over base editing.

responses.point: Aqvist offers to shift away from the PROTAC credit if the cereblon molecular-glue lineage is the mature core, and says Target-AID priority should be stated explicitly and not assumed.
responses.response: I agree that priority should be stated and not assumed, and I appreciate that you question your own B009 attribution. My round-1 view stands: the glue branch is on firmer ground than the PROTAC branch, but neither has an approved drug that defines the field, so I would still defer B009. I also would not cut B024 to Liu alone to make room for it; your own maturity caveat is the reason I do not follow you into the pairing.

uncertainties: Whether the documented record shows Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) ahead of, or level with, Komor et al. 2016 and Gaudelli et al. 2017, and whether that changes the three names or only the citation.
Whether the committee accepts first-author trainees in a Liu-led programme as laureates; if not, I would accept Liu alone as the fallback, but only for a prize the committee has argued for.
Whether base editing is seen as a follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether the evolved deaminase and editor architecture are accepted as the chemistry.
Whether B013 can be recognised in a later year once credit among the Vancouver, MIT and industrial lines is separable, and whether the cellular evidence for condensates (B047) stabilises.
statement.conflict_note: My earlier disclosure stands: my research field (lipid self-assembly, membrane phase behaviour, lipid-protein co-assembly) is scientifically close to B013 and B047, which I now list only as alternatives. I have no personal, institutional or collaborative connection to any credited name on B024, and I request no recusal. Sitting with Lund colleagues Linke and Somfai is not a candidate conflict.
